locator.section: VI.B Results, Long-Run Incidence, final sentence

correction: If the sentence is intended as a description of the cited study’s allocation estimate, distinguish the total non-consumer side from owner gains. The 2020 JPE paper analyses price, profit and markup asymmetries; its French subsection specifically studies price patterns. The related 2019 four-group analysis estimates owners at 57.7%, 62.4% and 55.7% after 6, 18 and 30 months, with workers and suppliers receiving separate shares. These are study estimates and stated lower-bound interpretations, not a correction establishing the actual owner share.
effect: Not an admitted error. A demonstrated allocation misdescription would weaken the particular owner-concentration argument; it would not overturn low consumer pass-through, owners being the largest beneficiaries, or the critique of untargeted sector support.
limits: The2019study expressly warns it may underestimate owner gains; no claim actual80%is statistically ruled out. This is a potential misdescription of what cited research establishes, not a refutation of an uncertain economic estimate or forecast for Germany. The author may have used owners loosely for the broader producer side; that reading would not accurately distinguish workers and suppliers but is preserved. No intent inferred.
materiality_explanation: Potentially minor if established: a sizeable allocation difference concerns a supporting distributional argument while the main limited-pass-through and targeting arguments survive. No materiality claim establishes that an error exists.
direction_explanation: True narrowly if the source-description finding is admitted: concentrating80%in owners strengthens the objection to this form of support.
